newsitem.title: FRANCE: Far-right French mayor gets police protection.
newsitem.headline: Far-right French mayor gets police protection.

text.p: The extreme-right mayor of the French Riviera port of Toulon, who is also the only National Front member of parliament, said on Saturday he had been given police protection after unspecified threats.
Jean-Marie le Chevallier, a member of Jean-Marie Le Pen's anti-immigrant party, said the protection was ordered by new Socialist Interior Minister Jean-Pierre Chevenement earlier this week.

"I haven't been given any explanations. But if the Interior Minister has taken these measures it's because there were serious risks for my security," he said. A magistrate had also been entrusted with a probe of the threats.

Le Chevallier, elected to parliament on June 1, noted that local parliamentarian Yann Piat, a member of the centrist UDF party, was killed in 1993 after she threatened to expose "Mafia-like" activities in the region.

Le Chevallier, one of only four Front mayors in France, said he had not personally received threats. "But we must be prudent, especially in the Var where there have already been political assassinations."
